newsitem.title: UK: British supermodel Campbell hits at colour prejudice.
newsitem.headline: British supermodel Campbell hits at colour prejudice.

text.p: Black supermodel Naomi Campbell hit out at colour prejudice in the fashion industry on Thursday, saying it was obsessed by blonde blue-eyed girls.
"There is prejudice and it's a problem," Campbell said in an interview in the Daily Telegraph newspaper. "I feel I have to speak out...make them more aware."
It was the glossy magazine industry that received the brunt of the British model's anger. The pigeon-holing of black models made it harder for them to get ahead, she said.

"It's more the people that run the magazines that are to blame," Campbell said, claiming she had been demoted to the inside cover of American Vogue last May in favour of another model after being promised the cover.
"This business is about selling and blonde and blue-eyed girls are what sells," she said.
During her 11-year career as a catwalk model, the 26-year-old Campbell has been dubbed the "black panther" and the "black Bardot".
"I was always called black something," Campbell said. "Of course I'm happy to be black. I'm proud of my colour. But some people think that by giving you a label they can put you in your place."
